Seriously who made a game with excruciatingly long dialogues alike of a royal decree .
Nope.

I don't see why this game is considered so intelligent. The writing is sophomorically obtuse, the pacing is glacially slow, and the range of meaningful choices available to your character is incredibly small. This is not an exciting creative vision. This is more like playing through that generic dream where you realize you've gone to school with no pants on.

I'm not much of a gamer, but I splashed out $15 on a sale copy of DE because I had seen so many people hype it up so hard and talk about it as though it was the communist masterpiece of the 21st century. I only logged 14.7 hours and spent most of that time stuck in areas of the map and quitting after 45 minutes due to migraines, disorientation, hand and wrist pain/fatigue and frustration. 

Here are some accessibility problems that I wish the devs had considered, from my own perspective as someone with chronic pain & mobility issues, chronic migraines & CTE:

- The initial setup screen features a fast/variable flicker effect, so I had to go through it as quickly as possible to avoid a worse migraine, and could not carefully consider skill allocation, which affected my gameplay and understanding of the game mechanics.
 
- The flickering effects throughout various parts of the game are a surefire instant migraine trigger.

- Not being able to zoom out to see the entire map & having more map features only available as an achievable bonus makes spatial orientation in the game very difficult.

- Having to manually walk characters around with no option for fast travel or teleporting causes hand & wrist fatigue very quickly, as well as spatial orientation issues. 

People kept telling me "it's supposed to be hard, that's the point", but I don't think it's supposed to be so hard that you can't enjoy it at all. I don't think it was supposed to take me 45 minutes to find the door out of Whirling-In-Rags. I somehow really doubt that's part of the intended experience. It's humiliating and sad to be excluded from such a wide-spanning media phenomenon just because your experiences are considered an edge case. 

I really wanted to like this game, but it doesn't seem like most developers are willing to do much to accommodate physical limitations, spatial orientation difficulties or photosensitivity. It's been so overhyped that I just feel bitter when I see people going on about how…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game features extensive reading and dialogue with no traditional combat mechanics.

citations.review_text:
+
• 3D | Isometric, semi-realistic art style
• tackles serious themes such as political ideologies, racism, extremism and the consequences of societal radicalization
• choices and dialogue have meaningful consequences
• classic RPG mechanics combined with skill and thought system
• deep, well-written dialogue 
• plenty of achievements
• no traditional combat; conflicts are resolved through conversations and skill checks

−
• despite focusing on themes that perfectly match my interests, the game never truly resonated with me emotionally

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
Disco Elysium is, without a doubt, an RPG that has been crafted with an incredible amount of thought and depth. It isn't afraid to tackle complex social and political issues, confronting players with questionable ideologies and the consequences of their own choices. Instead of relying on traditional combat, it offers a well-designed role-playing system centered around dialogue, decision-making, and character development.  It actually has everything I usually love in a game. I'm a huge fan of stories that critically examine political structures and socia systems. That made it all the more surprising that, despite all of its strengths, the game never truly clicked with me. I think one of the main reasons was that I never formed a genuine emotional connection with the 2 male protagonists. Because of that, I remained somewhat detached from the story, even though I can absolutely appreciate just how well-written and thoughtfully designed it is. I still give it a good review because, despite my not liking it, I still believe it is a good game.

_______________________

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the opening hours feel slow and act as a tedious barrier to entry before the game picks up.

citations.review_text:
5 years! (of this game stinking up my game library, [b]refunding it[/b] and then having it [i]gifted  back to me[/i]), multiple motivated attempts at fresh restarts & over 11hrs of my time wasted. I give up now.

I just can't get into this game whatsoever, the opening sequence on every single occasion is a monumental slog that is so slow and boring- my eyes begin to get heavy from the combination of exhaustive clicking, mindless roaming & listening to a horrible narration exacerbated with the plethora of miserable character conversations.

The writing really isn't worth all the praise it gets in my opinion; it tries to be witty, striking, bleak and nuanced but it just reeks of targeted admonishment for the player that has no understanding what the actual ♥♥♥♥ is going on in this communist plagued ♥♥♥♥ heap of a city.

Our main character is truly the worst part of all; he is honestly abhorrent with no sense of relatability whatsoever (unless you are a chronically depressed alcoholic with severe bouts of amnesia and hysteria) he is not likeable in the slightest. His myriad of actions leading up to and during the story, compounded with most of the possible dialogue options you can choose from just make him come across as a whimsical ♥♥♥♥♥♥ whom by the result of some sort of reality shattering cataclysmic event, lucked his way into becoming a police officer.

Confusing, directionless, pointless. This one of the most egregious experiences I have ever had in a video game. Simply awful.
First part was a drag, but once I got into the flow I've ended up enjoying a lot. Would recommend!
One of the best stories I've experienced. I do think the game can start off a bit slow, with the first 2 days but then it just absolutely picks up. Also Kim Kitsuragi.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game structure as resembling a visual novel or interactive book rather than a traditional game.

citations.review_text: I tried to like this game and was really excited based on all the praise it's received. Sadly, I just don't get this game. There seems to be very little actual game here, more like a VN with a lot of weird exposition.

3/5
Yeah so I didn't actually finish this game. I didn't love it, but I'm also turbo ADHD brained and a game that is pretty much a book that you sometimes click around in just isn't for me. But hey, even dropped/retired games teach you what you do and don't like.

I should add I really really wanted to like this game. So I'm pretty disappointed I couldn't finish it. But I bought it for like 3.59$ and played for 6.6 hours, so that's what ~$0.50 per hour played? What the ♥♥♥♥ can you do IRL at a price like that. So I'm happy with what I was able to get out of it.

If you are into games where you spend most of your time clicking around but are rewarded by complex storyline and meta narrative, I'd recommend it.

A game that tries very very hard to convince its players that its thought-provoking and interesting. It reuses the same sarcastic format over and over to try to seem informed about a myriad of social topics, yet barely actually discusses them. When it comes to the actual gameplay, it's a glorified visual novel with awful movement, awful fast traveling, and a stale RPG system. The worst thing, however, must be how overhyped this game is by its fans. I would recommend this game only if you really have an itch to play a detective game, but at that point you should just watch a show or read an actual book. This game is not deep, it's not complex. It has instead managed to fool those that can't see squabble for what it is.

I just don't understand all the reviews - they seem so incredible - 'critically acclaimed' - 'I wish I could play this again for the first time', the depth and exploration of blah blah

Am I missing something?  It is boring AF.  An elaborate point and click parading as an RPG? Damn, I am currently struggling with sunk/cost bias (15 hours in), I feel like I need to finish it or uninstall it

My initial frustration aside, the idea of the fractured mind talking to itself is refreshing, on top of this, the  voice acting is phenomenal, the music is also great. But.... this should have stayed a book or audiobook.

TL:DR overrated pretentious timewaste

The music also hits the game in Goty standards and is unforgettable. Just a warning though that some parts of the game like Martinaise's backstory is boring but the rest is amazing.

claims.claim: The game features fully voiced dialogue with standout performances specifically noted for the narrator skills and Kim Kitsuragi.

citations.review_text:
I can say with full confidence that a game like this will never come again.

The opening of the story completely hooked me and made me want to know more. And the game isn't afraid to go bold with political ideas and a world that's half-fallen apart, culturally and economically—it made me so curious to dig into what was left of it. The dialogue writing here is seriously TopTier, and the voice acting? Honestly indescribable. The world, the art style, the characters... and Kim Kitsuragi, the SideKick, deserves a whole paragraph on his own.

I can't recommend this game to everyone, but it's honestly a perfect experience

10/10

[h1]Everyone must experience Disco Elysium[/h1]
A while ago, a friend of mine recommended Disco Elysium to me, but I always put it off. Recently, however, I finally decided to give it a try...and I cannot believe what I've been missing out on for so long.
 
Many aspects of this game make it stand out: the incredible music by Sea Power (which I've already downloaded to my phone to listen to at work), the gorgeous art style and unique UI stylization, the detailed NPC portraits, the deep RPG elements, and the way side-quests intertwine to affect the main plot. However, the most notable feature is undoubtedly the voice acting. The original ZA/UM studio did a phenomenal job with the cast. Every character has their own highlight: distinct pronunciation, unique lexicons, and diverse accents, but the standout performances are Lenval Brown (the Narrator/Skills) and Julian Champenois (Kim Kitsuragi), who deliver one of the best performances I've ever heard in voice acting. The writing itself is what makes the game truly unforgettable - the skills constantly arguing in your head, the political and philosophical depth, and the way failure is often funnier and more interesting than success. Different builds and the four political alignments completely change the tone of the story, giving the deep RPG elements real replayability.

Another thing to highlight is the absence of useless achievements. Most developers like to pour them in just to have a lot of achievements.

I've always been fond of detective and noir/neo-noir stories, such as the 1997 Blade Runner game, which Disco Elysium delivers perfectly and scratches that part of my brain. If you are looking for an intriguing detective RPG with bold, unique artistic choices, then Disco Elysium is the game just for you!

Just be aware that it is very dialogue-heavy and a substantial playthrough, so go in ready for a long, text-rich experience.

and remember: [spoiler]HARDCORE TO THE MEGA![/spoiler]

I know I’m a bit late to the party. I didn't even become aware of this game until long after its release.

To be honest, I don't understand the legendary reviews it received—nor do I understand its classification as a role-playing game. It is no more of an RPG than GTA is a flight simulator, just because you can hop into a plane in that game, too.

It feels like a point-and-click adventure drowned in a sea of ​​text and added dice rolls. This whole mechanic is marketed as "fail forward," the idea being that a failure merely alters your path and leads to unexpected situations. However, this only works halfway, as there are situations where you simply hit a dead end.

Clothing affects your attributes. Yet, you never know beforehand which specific attribute you’ll need during a dialogue (and the game consists almost entirely of dialogues). Consequently, this feature is more or less pointless unless you flip the script and accept that the game adapts to your attributes rather than the other way around. But I don't see any sense in that.

The content itself is a wild hodgepodge of crime fiction, politics, and esotericism—unfortunately, none of it feels cohesive.

The story itself feels rather inconsequential and seems arbitrarily constructed merely to provide specific trigger points for the talent checks.

In my view, the art style, the repetitive soundtrack that plays in every location, and the incredibly sluggish pacing make this game impossible to recommend.

Incredible game! I enjoyed every second of it!
NO SPOILERS!!!
The story itself was very well written, the art was amazingly beautiful! The whole script with the all 24 skills is so well done I just can't imagine how much time costed the developing team to think of every possibility for a path a player can walk though! The character design was very good, especially I love the writing of Kim Kitsuragi, also love the great duo of him and the main character! They can be the funniest and the most serious team in the world!
The politisian systems were very well explained and love how the human society interprets them in their own way depending on their own lives.
The music was so interesting, because it sounded like a nostalgia most of the time with very unique detailes for the different places.
The voice acting was incredible, showing very well how a real conversation would go on!

All in all, in some strange way this game felt very real, emotional and mysterious for me and I totally recommend it for a new player to go through it without spoilers, do whatever you want in the game, everything is possible! 

Definitely will play it for second time after a short break!

I can't recommend this game, there are too many things that bothered me. First a couple positive points
+ The characters are very interesting, varied, each with their own motivations and personality.
+ Dice rolls are interesting way how to introduce some randomness, not just passing everything on first try.
+ The detective work is great, not only solving the murder but also trying to figure out things related with the main character's amnesia.
+ The voice acting is great.

And here are the negatives:
The UI and systems:
- The game gives you a lot of different items which help you with different skill checks. But you don't know before speaking to someone, which load out you will need and it can't be changed during the dialogue. Meaning you need to cancel the dialogue, put on appropriate clothing to make passing the check easier. It would also be helpful if you could click on a skill and it would equip the items that improve your chances automatically.
- The "internalization of memories" is a terrible system and should be removed. You have no idea what reward you will receive from the memory, and you can't remove it without using a skill point upgrade.
- There are too many skills to choose from, most of them are quite underwhelming.
- During my first playthrough, I picked the Thinker character, which means you will get a lot of exposition about history, biology, politics, geography, races... These things will be dumped on you constantly and it does not pertain to the story at hand at all.
- The map is useless and the fast travel only works from specific points and only sometimes.

The story:
- Many story threads were not closed properly or did not matter.
- The story is linear, you have no agency and there is no replayability.
- The ending of the game is very underwhelming, the murder mystery finishes in a very unsatisfying way.
- The amnesia of the main character is not resolved in a satisfying way either.

All in all, I had bigger expectations based on all the posit…

Every character has their own highlight: distinct pronunciation, unique lexicons, and diverse accents, but the standout performances are Lenval Brown (the Narrator/Skills) and Julian Champenois (Kim Kitsuragi), who deliver one of the best performances I've ever heard in voice acting. The writing itself is what makes the game truly unforgettable - the skills constantly arguing in your head, the political and philosophical depth, and the way failure is often funnier and more interesting than success. Different builds and the four political alignments completely change the tone of the story, giving the deep RPG elements real replayability.

Another thing to highlight is the absence of useless achievements. Most developers like to pour them in just to have a lot of achievements.

I've always been fond of detective and noir/neo-noir stories, such as the 1997 Blade Runner game, which Disco Elysium delivers perfectly and scratches that part of my brain. If you are looking for an intriguing detective RPG with bold, unique artistic choices, then Disco Elysium is the game just for you!

Just be aware that it is very dialogue-heavy and a substantial playthrough, so go in ready for a long, text-rich experience.

and remember: [spoiler]HARDCORE TO THE MEGA![/spoiler]

It's everything everyone has said before. I struggle to say something original or unique about Disco Elysium, but it is a great game if you enjoy reading and roleplaying, which can easily be compromised if you decide to save scum or become a completionist. You walk around, you decide how you want to behave in this world starting from a shell of a former character, and you basically exist while also trying to solve a murder case. The whole gameplay is dialogue, and deciding which thoughts and skills to invest your hard-earned points on for the chance to unlock different conversation paths.

And it is incredible at that. The writing is of course the highlight, but I could not forget the voice acting, which is probably the best I've seen in a videogame, or at least in the Top 3. I literally cannot get EGG HEAD yelling HARD-CORE from my head

Instead of focusing on the highlights, I'll just point out two things I thought worked pretty poorly. The first is the Skill Check Lock system, which prevented me from experiencing two storylines I was invested into. Basically if you fail a White Check, you can retry it after investing points on your skill. I failed a 97% Suggestion with Lilienne and already had reached my 6-point cap in that skill, making it impossible to progress in that storyline. Maybe I could have forgotten old Thoughts, learned a new one, and increased my cap, but I could not know which one until I've done so and I didn't have so much free time and points around. A similar thing happened when doing the nightclub quest, where I failed the Physical Instrument check to open the fridge and had already hit my learning cap, effectively locking me out of a very interesting quest. I was still able to beat the game, but it left me a sour taste that the game softlocked me out of these quests - either give me alternative routes to progress, or give me a permanent fail state, but don't give me this partial failure that I'm unable to act on.

claims.claim: Players describe the user interface and clothing system as clunky and laborious because equipping items to pass skill checks requires interrupting active dialogues.

citations.review_text:
I can't recommend this game, there are too many things that bothered me. First a couple positive points
+ The characters are very interesting, varied, each with their own motivations and personality.
+ Dice rolls are interesting way how to introduce some randomness, not just passing everything on first try.
+ The detective work is great, not only solving the murder but also trying to figure out things related with the main character's amnesia.
+ The voice acting is great.

And here are the negatives:
The UI and systems:
- The game gives you a lot of different items which help you with different skill checks. But you don't know before speaking to someone, which load out you will need and it can't be changed during the dialogue. Meaning you need to cancel the dialogue, put on appropriate clothing to make passing the check easier. It would also be helpful if you could click on a skill and it would equip the items that improve your chances automatically.
- The "internalization of memories" is a terrible system and should be removed. You have no idea what reward you will receive from the memory, and you can't remove it without using a skill point upgrade.
- There are too many skills to choose from, most of them are quite underwhelming.
- During my first playthrough, I picked the Thinker character, which means you will get a lot of exposition about history, biology, politics, geography, races... These things will be dumped on you constantly and it does not pertain to the story at hand at all.
- The map is useless and the fast travel only works from specific points and only sometimes.

The story:
- Many story threads were not closed properly or did not matter.
- The story is linear, you have no agency and there is no replayability.
- The ending of the game is very underwhelming, the murder mystery finishes in a very unsatisfying way.
- The amnesia of the main character is not resolved in a satisfying way either.

All in all, I had bigger expectations based on all the posit…

I'm on the fence with this, and don't recommend it overall though it is far from being a terrible experience. The issues with the game can be split in to mechanics and UX problems for me.

On the UX, this is simple... it's clunky. Fast travel is inconsistent as to when it works or not, having to constantly swap your clothing if you want to achieve the best results is a laborious process unless you can memorise what every item you've picked up does to your stats. Walking is slow, and running means constantly double clicking. Conversation trees seem to be incomplete at times even though they are, white skill checks remain in view even when they no longer exist, and when trying to track them down you have to also remember what conversational route you need to take to re-try the check. Over the entire game experience it felt like I had to work hard against the game's UI design to get to do what I wanted.

Game mechanics, and the game design. This is not an RPG, at least not anything other than a lite version of one. There are point-and-click adventures decades older than this that feel more dynamic. Rather than the skill system feeling like a way to boost your avenues of investigation, they frequently feel like they are instead there to remind you that you're not allowed to do things. Some skills are very clearly more important than others by the time the game ends, and as such the type of ending you have is determined by the upgrade path you take, not by the choices you make in conversation. There is a massive illusion of choice in this game as you are railroaded through most parts of the game, with very little consequence as to how you choose to go through certain conversations.

If this is an RPG, it is a TTRPG where the GM has already decided what's going to happen regardless of what skill checks you make, or decisions you take. The writing is in depth, but heavy, and again inconsequential. If you enjoy world building then you will no doubt be immersed by the prose.…

I know I’m a bit late to the party. I didn't even become aware of this game until long after its release.

To be honest, I don't understand the legendary reviews it received—nor do I understand its classification as a role-playing game. It is no more of an RPG than GTA is a flight simulator, just because you can hop into a plane in that game, too.

It feels like a point-and-click adventure drowned in a sea of ​​text and added dice rolls. This whole mechanic is marketed as "fail forward," the idea being that a failure merely alters your path and leads to unexpected situations. However, this only works halfway, as there are situations where you simply hit a dead end.

Clothing affects your attributes. Yet, you never know beforehand which specific attribute you’ll need during a dialogue (and the game consists almost entirely of dialogues). Consequently, this feature is more or less pointless unless you flip the script and accept that the game adapts to your attributes rather than the other way around. But I don't see any sense in that.

The content itself is a wild hodgepodge of crime fiction, politics, and esotericism—unfortunately, none of it feels cohesive.

The story itself feels rather inconsequential and seems arbitrarily constructed merely to provide specific trigger points for the talent checks.

In my view, the art style, the repetitive soundtrack that plays in every location, and the incredibly sluggish pacing make this game impossible to recommend.

Disco Elysium is something else. It's not a game. It's more like a book with choices, dice rolls and visuals. I got it because of the hype around it, suffered through the most part because it's slow, frustrating and boring, got intrigued enough to keep going and have now finished it. 
Were those 34 hours worth it? No, for me, they weren't. Most of the time I was bored, just interrupted by a few funny sequences and puzzle solving in my head. Yes, you have so many choices, but I hated that because every dialogue and scene were so dragged out, that it was no fun for me to explore them. Combined with the 'go figure' attitude regarding its systems that just felt like work. 
But I have to admit: the world, the characters, the story are somewhat great and there are tense and emotional moments, that I did not expect to hit so hard. And it is very mature in a subtle way, beyond the bad language, the jokes and the ol' communism vs. capitalism schtick.
Still, I can't flat recommend this. It's like a good book, that is way too drawn out. Try it out, see if you like it. And if not, toss it out.

claims.claim: Reviewers advise against purchasing the game on Steam due to controversies involving the original developers and company leadership.

citations.review_text:
[h1]GAME IS PEAK, DONT BUY IT!!!!!!!!!![/h1]

ZA/UM, the studio behind Disco Elysium, underwent a hostile corporate takeover, the ouster of its core creative founders, and multiple project cancellations and layoffs

Lead designer Robert Kurvitz, art director Aleksander Rostov, and writer Helen Hindpere were forced out of ZA/UM in late 2021, a departure publicly revealed in late 2022

Planned projects, including a Disco Elysium sequel (codenamed Y12) and a spin-off (X7), were canceled. ZA/UM pushed forward and released Zero Parades: For Dead Spies, but after it underperformed commercially, the studio issued layoffs affecting over 30 employees.

[h1] SOMETHING BEAUTIFUL IS GOING TO HAPPEN [/h1]

amazing, brilliant game that I cannot recommend you spend money on due to the creatives who made this game what it is being forced out of the company by shareholders. please play this if you can get it for free, just do not spend money on it because that money isn't going to the people who deserve it. thankfully I was gifted this game.

“It's the people on top – the motherf****s in sailing shoes and bowties – that f****d Harry, f****d Kim, f****d Robert, Rostov, Helen, Olga, Cash, f****d Elysium, f****d you and me too. They are not artists, they are professional f*****s.” - Argo Tuulik, one of the games writers.

Don't buy the game, pirate it. Don’t support ZA/UM, they stole the game from its original creators and they are profiting off of it.

But the game is a masterpiece. 1000/10

so incredible, I adore this game but please do not support the company if possible! bootleg, second-hand, pirate, whatever works best (outside investors fired the devs and now run the company), for the love of all things disco
this game is one of the best i've ever played. don't buy it on steam. don't support ZA/UM.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe a recent automatic update that forces promotional advertisements into the title and pause screens.

citations.review_text: WTH did they just force-install on my machine? Zero description, zero patch notes, incredibly shady behavior.

An absolutely incredible game that was stolen from the original creators. ZA/UM is now an evil company who is profiting greatly off the game they stole while the original devs who actually made the amazing piece of art that Disco Elysium is aren't seeing a penny and have been royally screwed by ZA/UM

And ZA/UM has the absolute GALL to plaster ads for their rip-off "spiritual successor" game, Zero Parades For Dead ZA/UM Exec-- I mean, Dead Spies,  on the title and pause screens for this game-- forced into your game through this most recent update (an update, which by the way, fixes ABSOLUTELY NOTHING, just forces you to look a their stupid ads without fixing any of the bugs in the game). You can't even roll it back. It's disgusting.

I would recommend playing this game to everyone and anyone-- it is an emotional experience left me a changed person, and it is a unique and incredible game. It may very well be my favorite. However, ZA/UM's behavior has been incredibly shameful with the way they're trying to milk this game for every last cent and their greed is straight-up embarrassing. So, while I recommend playing this game, I would not recommend buying this game from ZA/UM and giving the greedy ****s any more undeserved money, not if you can help it. If nothing else, please don't buy this game at full price haha.
